pr_title: lsp-config: Allow setting a server's environment variables
pr_comments: We require contributors to sign our Contributor License Agreement, and we don't have @davidbarsky on file. You can sign our CLA at https://zed.dev/cla. Once you've signed, post a comment here that says '@cla-bot check'.

Thanks for the contribution! This is just a nit but could you elaborate on the first bullet of the release notes with an example, like what was done in #9293.

We probably want to add a section to the language server docs on zed.dev to mention setting custom path/args/env, but we can do that in a followup PR and for now the release nodes and settings auto-complete are good enough.

@P1n3appl3 yup! updated the release notes post-merge.

@SomeoneToIgnore stdout is not available when using a language server in typical configurations, yes. It _would_ be available if the language server connected over TCP, but that's not a common configuration.

issue_context.title: extraEnv in rust-anaylzer to define rustflags
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

In vscode version rust-analyzer, you can specify env in `rust-analyzer.cargo.extraEnv` to define rustflags to be used while analyzing workspace.

How can I specify rustflags in zed?

https://rust-analyzer.github.io/manual.html

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


_No response_
comments:
Zed uses something similar but with a more convoluted syntax due to historic reasons unfortunately.
https://zed.dev/docs/languages/rust has some examples, and similar section could be created for cargo.
@SomeoneToIgnore Is there any way to define rustflags for `rust-analyzer.server.extraEnv` or `rust-analyzer.cargo.extraEnv` currently?
This prevents working on wasm projects which use the `web_sys_unstable_apis` flag, because the analyzer bails out on the use of those unstable features / classes.

Okay, I could make it work by setting the correct `RUSTFLAGS` as an env variable in the terminal and then starting zed from there.

(To be more precise, I was using a `shell.nix` which sets up the environment. I added a setting for `RUSTFLAGS` there.)

I'm running into this while trying to work on tokio in Zed. I need to work on stuff with `--cfg tokio_unstable`, and am having trouble getting rust-analyzer to be passed that environment variable.

Is it possible to do this, or will I need to avoid zed for now when developing on tokio?

@Noah-Kennedy we seem to use `tokio_unstable` ourselves with config.toml https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/fef567bb4984cf55d1e354d4f07ca10425e4613c/.cargo/config.toml#L3; I haven't heard any complaints from my peers, so maybe you could give that a go?

> [@Noah-Kennedy](https://github.com/Noah-Kennedy) we seem to use `tokio_unstable` ourselves with config.toml
> 
> [zed/.cargo/config.toml](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/fef567bb4984cf55d1e354d4f07ca10425e4613c/.cargo/config.toml#L3)
> 
> Line 3 in [fef567b](/zed-industries/zed/commit/fef567bb4984cf55d1e354d4f07ca10425e4613c)
>  rustflags = ["-C", "symbol-mangling-version=v0", "--cfg", "tokio_unstable"] 
> ; I haven't heard any complaints from my peers, so maybe you could give that a go?

It doesn't work for me, not sure why.

I still get `rust-analyzer: code is inactive due to #[cfg] directives: tokio_unstable is disabled`
I have gotten this on three different computers while using `.cargo/config.toml` to specify the relevant RUSTFLAGS invocations.

@Noah-Kennedy We still might not be picking up flags from `.cargo/config.toml`, but for now as a workaround you can add RUSTFLAGS under `lsp.rust-analyzer.env` in your settings, and if you'd like to do that per-project you can use a `.zed/settings.json` file in that workspace.

review_comments: I agree with removing this, having `stderr: ` on every output line isn't helpful unless we're interleaving it with other output and you need to be able to differentiate. @SomeoneToIgnore it looks like you were the one that added this, do you know if there's any other output here?

IIRC, stdout is not available to use at all when working with langservers?

So, no good reason to keep it here, was added during moving another code around and if the above is true, it's pretty useless.
